cards.text: At that time, the LORD speaks to Joshua, Israel's leader. He tells Joshua to make knives and circumcise the sons of Israel once again.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua what the knives should be made of. He says: make ___ knives.
Joshua does what the LORD says. He makes the knives and circumcises the sons of Israel.

cards.text: Now the passage stops to explain why. All the men of war who came out of Egypt had died on the journey through the wilderness.

cards.question: The men who came out of Egypt had all been circumcised. What about the sons born in the wilderness on the journey?

answers.text: None of them had been circumcised
Only the firstborn had been circumcised
Most had been circumcised on the way

cards.text: Israel wandered in the wilderness forty years, until all those men of war were gone. Forty YEARS. I spent a few years in a junk drawer and thought I was the world champion of waiting.

cards.question: Why did the men of war who came out of Egypt die in the wilderness?

answers.text: They did not obey the LORD
They were struck down by Egypt's army
They ran out of food on the journey

cards.question: Before they died, the LORD let those men of war see the land He had sworn to their fathers to give.

cards.text: So the LORD raised up their sons in their place. They're the ones Joshua circumcises, because nobody circumcised them along the way.

cards.question: After the whole nation has been circumcised, what does Israel do next?

answers.text: Stay in camp until they are healed
Cross back over the Jordan River

cards.text: Then the LORD says to Joshua, "Today I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you." Friend, when I finally got pulled out of the back of that junk drawer, I had so much dust on me that my dust had dust.

cards.question: Because the LORD rolled away the reproach of Egypt, that place has been called ___ to this day.

cards.text: It's the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, and the Israelites are camped at Gilgal on the plains of Jericho. And this is no ordinary evening.

cards.question: On that evening at Gilgal, the Israelites keep the ___.
The day after the Passover, what do the Israelites eat?

answers.text: Unleavened bread and roasted grain from the land
Bread they had carried all the way from Egypt
Grain they had bought from the people of Jericho

cards.text: Then, one day later, something changes. Something Israel has counted on for a LONG time.

cards.question: The day after Israel eats from the produce of the land, what stops?
With no more manna, the Israelites have nothing to eat that year.

cards.text: That year, Israel eats the crops of the land of Canaan. Stick around, friend, because this story is FAR from done.

findings.problem: The passage opens with "At that time," in the middle of the Jordan crossing story. The opening card repeats "At that time" but never says what time that is. It should say that Israel has just crossed the Jordan into Canaan.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences. It says who is speaking, to whom, and what is going on. If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke does not match the moment. In the verse, the LORD rolls away the reproach of Egypt. The joke is about Papa Dorin being covered in dust, not about anything being removed, so it lands as a non sequitur. It also adds to his backstory. In his story, the angel renews him and he stands clean on his gold base. He is never "pulled out" of the drawer covered in dust.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The dusty "pulled out" moment contradicts and adds to the Dorinverse backstory. There, the drawer is gone in the blink of an eye and he is renewed with a clean apron.

rule.text: His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them.

findings.problem: The right answer "The manna" is much shorter than the wrong answers "The pillar of cloud" and "The water from the rock."

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain narration with little of Papa Dorin's voice, for example cards 1, 4, 9 and 13 ("Now the passage stops to explain why."). Card 6 has the only real joke that works. The walkthrough reads like a pleasant narrator, not laugh-out-loud Papa Dorin.

rule.text: Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
